deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a mathematical derivation. It is a descriptive crystallography (mineralogy) note in the classification style of Weiss and Naumann, probably lecture notes; the context (Weiss'sche Nomenclatur, Abstumpfung/Zuschärfung on the next page) shows this. It lists octahedral and rhombohedral 'Grundformen' by crystal system and counts the kinds of faces, edges, vertices and plane angles.

The statements, restated in modern terms (vertex coordinates are mine, used only to check the counts):

(3) Rhombenoktaeder (orthorhombic dipyramid). Vertices are ±a·e1, ±b·e2, ±c·e3 with a, b, c distinct. The 8 faces are congruent scalene triangles.

(4) Rectangular octahedron. Base is a rectangle with corners (±p, ±q, 0); the apices are (0, 0, ±h). There are two kinds of faces, all isosceles: those on the long base side and those on the short side.

(5) Rhomboidal octahedron. Base is a parallelogram with vertices ±A, ±B (not perpendicular, unequal length); the apices are ±h·e3.
- Faces: two kinds.
- Edges: four kinds. Two kinds of lateral edges, of lengths sqrt(|A|²+h²) and sqrt(|B|²+h²). Two kinds of base edges, |A−B| and |A+B| (the 'greater' and 'smaller' Grundkanten).
- Vertices: three kinds (apices, ±A, ±B).
- Plane angles: 6 distinct, i.e. 2 scalene face types × 3 angles.

Second division: the base lies in an inclined, not horizontal, plane (oblique axis; monoclinic and triclinic).

(1) Klinorhombic octahedron (monoclinic). Base is a rhombus in inclined position. Under the 2/m symmetry the 8 lateral edges fall into 3 orbits: {c–a, −c–(−a)}, {c–(−a), −c–a}, and the 4 edges to ±b. Hence '3 kinds of lateral/middle edges'. All base edges are equal.

(2) Klinorhomboidic octahedron (triclinic, only a centre of symmetry). Base is a parallelogram. There are 4 kinds of faces, all scalene triangles. Edges form 6 inversion pairs: 4 kinds of lateral edges and 2 kinds of base edges.

IV. Abtheilung: Rhombohedron. It is bounded by 6 congruent rhombi and has 2 kinds of vertices:
- 2 polar vertices whose three plane angles are equal;
- 6 lateral vertices with two equal angles and one unequal.

The edges meeting at the polar vertices are named Pol-/End-(?)kanten; the next page continues: the others are 'Grundkanten'.

The page contains no calculation, only combinatorial and symmetry counts.
errors: No substantive errors; every count checks out by symmetry-orbit counting.

Minor terminological looseness: the rhombohedron's edges at the polar vertices are usually called Polkanten/Endkanten and the zigzag edges Randkanten/Mittelkanten. The transcribed 'Mittelkanten' for the polar edges is probably a transcription problem, not Riemann's error.

results.what: Counts of face, edge, vertex and plane-angle types for rhombic, rectangular, rhomboidal, monoclinic and triclinic octahedra and for the rhombohedron
results.modern_name: Crystal forms (dipyramids, rhombohedron) and their symmetry orbits in the orthorhombic, monoclinic, triclinic and trigonal systems
results.usually_credited_to: C. S. Weiss (1815) and F. Mohs / C. F. Naumann (1820s–1830s); standard 19th-century mineralogy textbook material

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine student or lecture notes on descriptive crystallography following the Weiss/Naumann classification. There is no original mathematics; it is only of minor biographical interest that Riemann attended or noted mineralogy lectures.

checkable.asserts: In the rhomboidal octahedron the two base-edge lengths and the two lateral-edge lengths are distinct, giving 4 kinds of edges.

checkable.asserts: The rhomboidal octahedron has 6 distinct plane angles (expected value 6).
At a polar vertex of a rhombohedron spanned by three equal-length edge vectors with equal mutual angles, all three plane angles are equal.
The faces of the rhombic octahedron are scalene triangles (three different side lengths).
